default.irrigation: Irrigate according to soil moisture and crop stage; avoid both drought stress and waterlogging.
default.nutrients: Base fertilizer on a soil test; apply phosphorus and potassium before planting and split nitrogen during active growth.
default.pests: Scout weekly and use integrated pest management before considering a labelled pesticide.
default.weather: Check the forecast before irrigation and spraying; provide drainage before heavy rain.
default.weeds: Keep the crop weed-free during establishment and early flowering; mulch or intercrop where suitable.

apple.irrigation: Use drip irrigation; maintain even moisture from fruit set through fruit enlargement and reduce irrigation before harvest.
apple.nutrients: Apply compost and soil-test-based potassium; split nitrogen between bud break and fruit set rather than overfeeding.
apple.pests: Monitor codling moth, aphids and scab; use pheromone traps, sanitation and registered controls when thresholds are reached.
apple.weather: Protect blossoms from late frost and maintain airflow; avoid overhead irrigation during wet, cool periods.
apple.weeds: Keep a weed-free strip around trees and use organic mulch without touching the trunk.

banana.irrigation: Provide frequent drip or basin irrigation during bunch development; maintain drainage because roots are sensitive to standing water.
banana.nutrients: Supply potassium in split applications with compost and balanced nitrogen; avoid placing fertilizer against the pseudostem.
banana.pests: Remove damaged leaves and monitor banana weevil, thrips and nematodes; use clean planting material and IPM.
banana.weather: Stake or brace plants before storms and protect bunches from sun and wind where needed.
banana.weeds: Mulch the basin and control weeds shallowly to protect the surface root system.

blackgram.irrigation: Give light irrigation at branching, flowering and pod filling; stop excess watering near maturity.
blackgram.nutrients: Use seed inoculation and a small starter nitrogen dose; prioritize phosphorus and sulfur based on soil test.
blackgram.pests: Scout for whitefly, aphids and pod borer; remove infected plants and use neem or registered IPM options.
blackgram.weather: Provide raised drainage in rainy periods and avoid sowing before prolonged wet weather.
blackgram.weeds: Control weeds within the first 20-30 days with one timely interculture or approved herbicide.

chickpea.irrigation: Prefer well-drained soil; irrigate at branching, flowering and pod filling only when moisture is limiting.
chickpea.nutrients: Inoculate seed with appropriate rhizobia and apply phosphorus and sulfur from a soil test; avoid excess nitrogen.
chickpea.pests: Monitor gram pod borer with pheromone traps and scout flowers and pods; conserve beneficial insects.
chickpea.weather: Avoid waterlogging and late heavy irrigation because cool, wet foliage increases disease risk.
chickpea.weeds: Keep fields clean during the first 6 weeks with shallow interculture to avoid root damage.

coconut.irrigation: Deeply irrigate the basin during dry months and mulch heavily; ensure rapid drainage during monsoon.
coconut.nutrients: Apply compost and palm fertilizer in a wide ring away from the trunk, timed before reliable rainfall.
coconut.pests: Inspect the crown for rhinoceros beetle and red palm weevil; use pheromone traps and remove breeding material.
coconut.weather: Support young palms against wind and maintain drainage around the root zone.
coconut.weeds: Keep a mulched basin weed-free and use cover crops between palms where moisture permits.

coffee.irrigation: Maintain mulch and irrigate during flowering and berry expansion when rainfall is insufficient; avoid saturation.
coffee.nutrients: Use compost plus split nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium applications after soil and leaf testing.
coffee.pests: Monitor coffee berry borer, leaf rust and white stem borer; improve shade, sanitation and targeted IPM.
coffee.weather: Maintain filtered shade and windbreaks; avoid wetting foliage late in the day.
coffee.weeds: Use mulch and shallow slashing; avoid deep hoeing around feeder roots.

cotton.irrigation: Irrigate at square formation, flowering and boll development; avoid excess water during boll opening.
cotton.nutrients: Apply phosphorus and potassium basally and split nitrogen before flowering; avoid late excessive nitrogen.
cotton.pests: Monitor bollworm and whitefly with pheromone and sticky traps; follow threshold-based IPM.
cotton.weather: Ensure drainage after heavy rain and avoid spraying during high wind or when rain is imminent.
cotton.weeds: Keep the field weed-free for the first 60 days and avoid damaging shallow roots during interculture.

grapes.irrigation: Use regulated drip irrigation; maintain moisture during berry set and enlargement and reduce water near ripening.
grapes.nutrients: Split fertigation by growth stage with emphasis on potassium during berry development; confirm with soil and leaf tests.
grapes.pests: Scout for powdery mildew, downy mildew and thrips; prune for airflow and use labelled fungicides only when needed.
grapes.weather: Train vines to improve ventilation and protect ripening bunches from rain splitting.
grapes.weeds: Maintain a clean strip below vines with mulch or shallow cultivation.

jute.irrigation: Maintain moisture during establishment and rapid stem growth; drain standing water after heavy rain.
jute.nutrients: Apply balanced nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium from a soil test; split nitrogen to prevent weak, lush stems.
jute.pests: Scout for semilooper and stem weevil; remove badly affected plants and use biological or registered controls.
jute.weather: Sow with reliable early moisture and avoid waterlogged seedbeds.
jute.weeds: Thin and weed early, especially during the first 4-6 weeks when seedlings grow slowly.

kidneybeans.irrigation: Give light irrigations at flowering and pod filling; avoid waterlogging and stop excess irrigation before harvest.
kidneybeans.nutrients: Inoculate seed where suitable and apply phosphorus and potassium; avoid heavy nitrogen that delays maturity.
kidneybeans.pests: Monitor bean aphid, pod borer and rust; use clean seed, crop rotation and threshold-based IPM.
kidneybeans.weather: Use well-drained beds and avoid field work when foliage is wet to reduce disease spread.
kidneybeans.weeds: Control weeds during the first 30-40 days with shallow cultivation.

lentil.irrigation: Usually needs limited irrigation; water at branching and pod filling only when soil moisture is low.
lentil.nutrients: Use rhizobium inoculation and soil-test-based phosphorus and sulfur; avoid excess nitrogen.
lentil.pests: Scout for aphids, pod borer and wilt; rotate crops and remove diseased plants promptly.
lentil.weather: Ensure drainage and avoid prolonged leaf wetness during flowering.
lentil.weeds: Keep seedlings weed-free through the first 6 weeks with timely shallow weeding.

maize.irrigation: Protect soil moisture at knee-high growth, tasseling, silking and grain filling; tasseling and silking are most sensitive.
maize.nutrients: Apply phosphorus and potassium at planting and split nitrogen between early growth and knee-high stage.
maize.pests: Scout for fall armyworm and stem borer in the whorl; use traps and targeted IPM based on infestation.
maize.weather: Provide drainage after heavy rain and avoid water stress around silking.
maize.weeds: Control weeds during the first 30-45 days and earth up carefully without damaging roots.

mango.irrigation: Reduce irrigation before flowering, then irrigate during fruit set and fruit enlargement; avoid waterlogging.
mango.nutrients: Apply compost and soil-test-based fertilizer after harvest; split nitrogen and potassium around flowering and fruit set.
mango.pests: Monitor hopper, mealybug and fruit fly; use orchard sanitation, traps and selective IPM.
mango.weather: Improve canopy airflow and protect blossoms from prolonged rain and strong wind.
mango.weeds: Keep a mulched, weed-free basin and mow inter-row cover rather than deep hoeing.

mothbeans.irrigation: Use limited irrigation at flowering and pod filling; the crop tolerates dry conditions but not standing water.
mothbeans.nutrients: Apply seed inoculation and soil-test-based phosphorus; avoid high nitrogen in low-rainfall fields.
mothbeans.pests: Scout for pod borer, aphids and mites; use crop rotation and threshold-based IPM.
mothbeans.weather: Use well-drained fields and avoid irrigation before forecast rain.
mothbeans.weeds: Complete one early weeding within 20-25 days to protect slow initial growth.

mungbean.irrigation: Irrigate lightly at flowering and pod filling when needed; stop before pods mature.
mungbean.nutrients: Use rhizobium inoculation and phosphorus and sulfur based on soil test; avoid excess nitrogen.
mungbean.pests: Monitor whitefly, thrips and pod borer; remove virus-affected plants and use selective IPM.
mungbean.weather: Provide drainage and avoid wet foliage during flowering and pod development.
mungbean.weeds: Keep the crop weed-free during the first 30 days with shallow interculture.

muskmelon.irrigation: Use drip irrigation; maintain even moisture during fruit set and enlargement and reduce water near ripening.
muskmelon.nutrients: Use compost and split fertigation with potassium during fruit development; avoid excess nitrogen.
muskmelon.pests: Scout for aphids, whitefly, fruit fly and powdery mildew; use nets, sanitation and labelled IPM.
muskmelon.weather: Use raised beds and mulch to keep fruit dry; protect vines from prolonged wet conditions.
muskmelon.weeds: Mulch after establishment and remove weeds without disturbing shallow vines.

orange.irrigation: Use deep, regular irrigation during fruit set and enlargement; allow the surface to dry slightly between watering.
orange.nutrients: Apply compost and citrus fertilizer in split doses, with potassium during fruit development and micronutrients after testing.
orange.pests: Monitor citrus psylla, leaf miner, scale and citrus canker; prune infected tissue and use IPM.
orange.weather: Maintain drainage and wind protection; avoid overhead irrigation to reduce disease.
orange.weeds: Keep a mulched weed-free basin without piling mulch against the trunk.

papaya.irrigation: Irrigate frequently but lightly with good drainage; maintain moisture during flowering and fruit filling.
papaya.nutrients: Apply compost and split nitrogen and potassium regularly; include boron and other micronutrients only after testing.
papaya.pests: Scout for papaya ringspot, mites and fruit fly; use clean seedlings, rouging and sanitation.
papaya.weather: Protect from wind and drain water quickly because papaya is highly sensitive to root rot.
papaya.weeds: Use shallow weeding and organic mulch around, but not touching, the stem.

pigeonpeas.irrigation: Usually rainfed; provide supplemental water at flowering and pod filling during extended dry spells.
pigeonpeas.nutrients: Inoculate seed and apply phosphorus and sulfur according to soil test; avoid excessive nitrogen.
pigeonpeas.pests: Monitor pod borer and pod fly with traps and regular flower and pod scouting.
pigeonpeas.weather: Use well-drained soil and avoid waterlogging during the long crop duration.
pigeonpeas.weeds: Keep rows weed-free for the first 45 days, then maintain clean inter-row space.

pomegranate.irrigation: Use drip irrigation with consistent moisture during flowering and fruit enlargement; avoid sudden wet-dry cycles.
pomegranate.nutrients: Apply compost and split nitrogen and potassium based on soil and leaf tests; avoid excess nitrogen.
pomegranate.pests: Monitor fruit borer, aphids and bacterial blight; remove damaged fruit and disinfect pruning tools.
pomegranate.weather: Prune for airflow and protect fruit from prolonged rain and cracking.
pomegranate.weeds: Maintain a clean, mulched basin and mow cover between rows.

rice.irrigation: Keep soil moist during establishment, use shallow alternate wetting and drying after establishment, and drain 7-10 days before harvest.
rice.nutrients: Apply phosphorus and potassium basally; split nitrogen at tillering and panicle initiation using a soil test.
rice.pests: Scout for blast, bacterial leaf blight, brown planthopper and stem borer; avoid excess nitrogen and use IPM.
rice.weather: Maintain field drainage during storms and avoid nitrogen or fungicide applications before heavy rain.
rice.weeds: Use stale seedbed, timely mechanical weeding or a locally approved herbicide during early crop growth.

watermelon.irrigation: Use drip irrigation with steady moisture through fruit set and enlargement; reduce irrigation as fruit ripens.
watermelon.nutrients: Use compost and split nitrogen with higher potassium during fruit filling; avoid excess nitrogen.
watermelon.pests: Scout for aphids, whitefly, mites, fruit fly and downy mildew; use mulch, sanitation and IPM.
watermelon.weather: Use raised beds and mulch to keep fruit dry and provide drainage during heavy rain.
watermelon.weeds: Mulch after vines establish and remove weeds shallowly to avoid damaging the root zone.
